title: What If Everyone on Earth Jumped at the Same Time?

scenes.text: What if all eight billion people jumped at the same moment? Earth would move. Barely.
All of us together weigh a few hundred million tonnes. Earth weighs six thousand billion billion.
The planet would shift by less than the width of a single atom, and bounce straight back.
To jump together we'd have to stand together: everyone fits in an area about the size of a large city.
Landing there would shake the ground like a small earthquake, and the roar would be the loudest sound ever made.
The real disaster comes after: eight billion people trying to get home from one city.

description:
What if everyone on Earth jumped at once?
Earth moves less than an atom's width and bounces back. The jump itself: a small local quake and the loudest sound ever. The real problem is the journey home.
What should we run through next?
